```{ojs}
//| output: false
// How far back the heatmap reaches.
changesWindowDays = 90

// A reading's direction is measured from the one before it, so the queries
// read this far past the window to find the first day's.
changesLookbackDays = 14
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
changesStates = {
  const seen = new Set();
  for (const station of filteredStations) {
    if (station.country === "US" && station.region) seen.add(station.region);
  }
  return [...seen].sort();
}

// State grain: one cell per (chain, state, day). `changed` says a price moved
// and not which way, so the rises and falls are counted here, against the same
// previous reading the flag was set from.
changesByState = db
  ? await db.query(`
      WITH priced AS (
        SELECT station_key, brand, capture_date, changed,
               price_local_per_litre - lag(price_local_per_litre) OVER (
                 PARTITION BY station_key ORDER BY capture_date
               ) AS delta
        FROM history
        WHERE grade = ${sqlText(grade)}${chainClause}
          AND capture_date > (SELECT max(capture_date) FROM history) - ${
            changesWindowDays + changesLookbackDays
          }
      ),
      scoped AS (
        SELECT p.brand, s.region, p.station_key, p.capture_date, p.changed, p.delta
        FROM priced p JOIN stations s ON s.station_key = p.station_key
        WHERE s.country = 'US' AND s.region IS NOT NULL
          AND p.capture_date > (SELECT max(capture_date) FROM history) - ${changesWindowDays}
      )
      SELECT brand,
             region,
             strftime(capture_date, '%Y-%m-%d') AS d,
             count(*) FILTER (WHERE changed IS NOT NULL)   AS n_obs,
             count(*) FILTER (WHERE changed)               AS n_changed,
             count(*) FILTER (WHERE changed AND delta > 0) AS n_up,
             count(*) FILTER (WHERE changed AND delta < 0) AS n_down,
             count(DISTINCT station_key)                   AS n_stations
      FROM scoped
      GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
      ORDER BY brand, region, d
    `)
  : []

// Station grain, for one state. station_key leads the parquet's sort order, so
// this prunes row groups rather than scanning.
changesStationKeys = {
  if (changesPlace === "All US states") return [];
  return filteredStations
    .filter((s) => s.country === "US" && s.region === changesPlace)
    .map((s) => s.station_key);
}

changesByStation = db && changesStationKeys.length
  ? await db.query(`
      WITH priced AS (
        SELECT station_key, brand, capture_date, changed,
               price_local_per_litre - lag(price_local_per_litre) OVER (
                 PARTITION BY station_key ORDER BY capture_date
               ) AS delta
        FROM history
        WHERE station_key IN (${sqlList(changesStationKeys)})
          AND grade = ${sqlText(grade)}
          AND capture_date > (SELECT max(capture_date) FROM history) - ${
            changesWindowDays + changesLookbackDays
          }
      )
      SELECT station_key,
             brand,
             strftime(capture_date, '%Y-%m-%d') AS d,
             count(*) FILTER (WHERE changed IS NOT NULL)   AS n_obs,
             count(*) FILTER (WHERE changed)               AS n_changed,
             count(*) FILTER (WHERE changed AND delta > 0) AS n_up,
             count(*) FILTER (WHERE changed AND delta < 0) AS n_down
      FROM priced
      WHERE capture_date > (SELECT max(capture_date) FROM history) - ${changesWindowDays}
      GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
      ORDER BY station_key, d
    `)
  : []
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Full date domain including gaps, so the axis stays honest about time.
function changesDomain(rows) {
  const days = rows.map((r) => r.d).filter((d) => d);
  if (!days.length) return [];
  const first = new Date(days.reduce((a, b) => (a < b ? a : b)) + "T00:00:00Z");
  const last = new Date(days.reduce((a, b) => (a > b ? a : b)) + "T00:00:00Z");
  const out = [];
  for (let t = new Date(first); t <= last; t.setUTCDate(t.getUTCDate() + 1)) {
    out.push(t.toISOString().slice(0, 10));
  }
  return out;
}

// The narrowest a day's cell is drawn. With less room than this a day, days
// are binned into weeks: a phone has a third of a desktop's width, and less
// again once a state's station names take their margin.
CHANGES_MIN_BIN_PX = 5

// The Monday of a day's week, written as a day is, so a week's bin sorts and
// labels like one.
function weekStart(day) {
  const d = new Date(day + "T00:00:00Z");
  d.setUTCDate(d.getUTCDate() - ((d.getUTCDay() + 6) % 7));
  return d.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
}

// Sums counts (not means of rates) so thin days don't get equal weight.
function changesBinned(rows, keyName, maxBins) {
  const domain = changesDomain(rows);
  const weekly = domain.length > maxBins;
  const bins = new Map();
  for (const row of rows) {
    const bin = weekly ? weekStart(row.d) : row.d;
    const key = [row[keyName], row.brand, bin].join(" :: ");
    const cell = bins.get(key) || {
      key: row[keyName],
      brand: row.brand,
      bin,
      n_obs: 0,
      n_changed: 0,
      n_up: 0,
      n_down: 0,
      n_stations: 0
    };
    cell.n_obs += Number(row.n_obs) || 0;
    cell.n_changed += Number(row.n_changed) || 0;
    cell.n_up += Number(row.n_up) || 0;
    cell.n_down += Number(row.n_down) || 0;
    cell.n_stations = Math.max(cell.n_stations, Number(row.n_stations) || 0);
    bins.set(key, cell);
  }
  const cells = [...bins.values()].map((cell) => {
    // A cell is colored on whatever readings it has: a station's row has one
    // a day, and so does a state with one station. A floor of three left
    // both gray. Only a cell with nothing to compare has no color.
    const told = cell.n_obs > 0;
    return {
      ...cell,
      rate: told ? cell.n_changed / cell.n_obs : null,
      net: told ? (cell.n_up - cell.n_down) / cell.n_obs : null
    };
  });
  const binDomain = weekly ? [...new Set(domain.map(weekStart))] : domain;
  return {cells, binDomain, weekly};
}

// Five steps from every reading falling to every reading rising. The middle
// one takes a cell within a fifth of even: prices that held, or as many up as
// down.
function colorForNet(net, pal) {
  if (net == null || !isFinite(net)) return pal.missing;
  const size = Math.abs(net);
  const step = size < 0.2 ? 0 : size < 0.6 ? 1 : 2;
  return pal.diverging[2 + Math.sign(net) * step];
}

// Plot sets a label in 10px system-ui. Measured rather than guessed at, so a
// name shortened to fit its margin does fit it.
labelWidth = {
  const context = document.createElement("canvas").getContext("2d");
  context.font = "10px system-ui, sans-serif";
  return (text) => context.measureText(text).width;
}

function changesDay(day) {
  return new Date(day + "T00:00:00Z").toLocaleDateString("en-US", {
    month: "short",
    day: "numeric",
    timeZone: "UTC"
  });
}

function changesCount(n, noun) {
  return `${n.toLocaleString()} ${noun}${n === 1 ? "" : "s"}`;
}
```


## How the price moved
::: {.cgp-panel}

```{ojs}
// Keyed on station_key, labelled by name.
function changesChart(
  rows,
  keyName,
  {rowLabel, mode, perStation, labelOf = (key) => key}
) {
  if (!rows.length) return null;
  // A chain's chart is headed with its name, so a row need not end in it.
  const rowName = new Map();
  for (const row of rows) {
    const name = labelOf(row[keyName]) || row[keyName];
    const chain = BRAND_NAMES[row.brand];
    rowName.set(
      row[keyName],
      chain && name.endsWith(" " + chain) ? name.slice(0, -chain.length - 1) : name
    );
  }
  // The margin holds the longest name, up to 45% of the chart's width and
  // always leaving the plot 140px; a name longer than that is cut to fit.
  const widest = Math.max(0, ...[...rowName.values()].map(labelWidth));
  const left = Math.min(
    Math.max(56, Math.ceil(widest + 12)),
    Math.max(56, Math.min(chartWidth - 24 - 140, Math.round(chartWidth * 0.45)))
  );
  const rowText = new Map(
    [...rowName].map(([key, name]) => {
      let text = name;
      while (text.length > 1 && labelWidth(text) > left - 12) {
        text = text.slice(0, -2).trimEnd() + "…";
      }
      return [key, text];
    })
  );
  const plotWidth = chartWidth - left - 24;
  const {cells, binDomain, weekly} = changesBinned(
    rows,
    keyName,
    Math.max(14, Math.floor(plotWidth / CHANGES_MIN_BIN_PX))
  );
  if (!cells.length) return null;
  // Plot labels every value of a band scale, and a phone has room for five.
  // Counted back from the newest bin, so that one is always named.
  const stride = Math.ceil(binDomain.length / Math.max(2, Math.floor(plotWidth / 56)));
  const dateTicks = binDomain.filter((_, i) => (binDomain.length - 1 - i) % stride === 0);
  const fillOf = (c) =>
    mode === "often" ? colorForFraction(c.rate, palette) : colorForNet(c.net, palette);
  const tipOf = (c) => {
    const head = `${rowName.get(c.key)} · ${weekly ? "week of " : ""}${changesDay(c.bin)}`;
    if (!c.n_obs) return `${head}\nno earlier reading to compare`;
    // One station's one reading is said in words; a state's are counted, so
    // a color that rests on a single station says so.
    if (perStation && c.n_obs === 1) {
      const way = c.n_down ? "fell" : c.n_up ? "rose" : "unchanged";
      return `${head}\n${way} since the previous reading`;
    }
    const held = c.n_obs - c.n_changed;
    return (
      `${head}\n${c.n_down} fell · ${c.n_up} rose\n${held} unchanged\n` +
      `of ${changesCount(c.n_obs, "reading")}`
    );
  };
  // A tip opens to one side of its cell and is cut off at the chart's edge,
  // so its lines wrap short enough to fit beside a cell in the middle.
  const tipLine = Math.max(9, Math.min(20, Math.floor((chartWidth / 2 - 40) / 12)));
  const brands = [...new Set(cells.map((c) => c.brand))].sort();

  const charts = brands.map((brand) => {
    const mine = cells.filter((c) => c.brand === brand);
    // Each chain's rows are its own set, sorted by label then key.
    const keys = [...new Set(mine.map((c) => c.key))].sort((a, b) => {
      const [x, y] = [rowName.get(a), rowName.get(b)];
      return x < y ? -1 : x > y ? 1 : a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0;
    });
    const top = 28;
    const bottom = 30;
    // Height = margins + one full pitch per row.
    const pitch = chartWidth < 520 ? 11 : 16;
    return Plot.plot({
      width: chartWidth,
      height: top + bottom + keys.length * pitch,
      marginLeft: left,
      marginRight: 24,
      marginTop: top,
      marginBottom: bottom,
      style: {background: "transparent", color: palette.text},
      x: {domain: binDomain, label: null, ticks: dateTicks, tickFormat: changesDay},
      y: {domain: keys, label: null, tickFormat: (key) => rowText.get(key)},
      ariaLabel: `${BRAND_NAMES[brand] || brand}: ${
        mode === "often" ? "how often" : "which way"
      } the posted ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]} price moved, by ${rowLabel}`,
      marks: [
        Plot.cell(mine, {
          x: "bin",
          y: "key",
          // A function fill gets an identity color scale, so these follow
          // Quarto's light/dark toggle the way the map's markers do.
          fill: fillOf,
          inset: 0.5
        }),
        // A tip rather than a `title`, which a touch screen never shows.
        Plot.tip(
          mine,
          Plot.pointer({x: "bin", y: "key", ...tipStyle(), lineWidth: tipLine, title: tipOf})
        ),
        Plot.text([BRAND_NAMES[brand] || brand], {
          frameAnchor: "top-left",
          dy: -14,
          fontWeight: 600,
          fill: palette.text
        })
      ]
    });
  });
  return {charts, weekly};
}

changesFigure = {
  if (!db) {
    return html`<div class="cgp-notice cgp-station-chart">Loading the price database…</div>`;
  }
  const drilled = changesPlace !== "All US states";
  const rows = drilled ? changesByStation : changesByState;
  if (!rows.length) {
    return html`<div class="cgp-notice">No ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]} history yet${
      drilled ? ` for ${changesPlace}` : ""
    }. This fills in as captures accumulate.</div>`;
  }
  const nameOf = new Map(filteredStations.map((s) => [s.station_key, s.name]));
  const drawn = changesChart(rows, drilled ? "station_key" : "region", {
    rowLabel: drilled ? "station" : "state",
    mode: changesMode,
    perStation: drilled,
    labelOf: drilled ? (key) => nameOf.get(key) || key : undefined
  });
  if (!drawn) return html`<div class="cgp-notice">Not enough readings yet.</div>`;
  // A station's cell for one day is one reading: it fell, held or rose.
  const single = drilled && !drawn.weekly;
  return html`<div>${changesKeyEl(changesMode, single)}${changesSummary}${drawn.charts}</div>`;
}

// Manual legend: Plot draws none for function fills, and tooltips are
// inaccessible on touch devices.
function changesKeyEl(mode, single) {
  const swatch = (color) =>
    html`<span class="cgp-swatch" style=${"background:" + color}></span>`;
  const missing = html`<span class="cgp-legend-missing">${swatch(
    palette.missing
  )} no earlier reading</span>`;
  if (mode === "often") {
    return html`<div class="cgp-legend cgp-changes-key">
      <span class="cgp-legend-end">0%</span>${palette.ramp.map(swatch)}<span
        class="cgp-legend-end">100%</span>
      <span class="cgp-legend-note">share of the readings in a cell where the posted price had
        moved since the station's previous reading</span>
      ${missing}
    </div>`;
  }
  const [fell, , flat, , rose] = palette.diverging;
  return html`<div class="cgp-legend cgp-changes-key">
    <span class="cgp-legend-end">${single ? "▼ Fell" : "▼ More fell"}</span>${(single
      ? [fell, flat, rose]
      : palette.diverging
    ).map(swatch)}<span class="cgp-legend-end">${single ? "Rose ▲" : "More rose ▲"}</span>
    <span class="cgp-legend-note">${
      single
        ? "whether the station's posted price fell, held or rose since its previous reading"
        : "the share of a cell's readings where the posted price rose since the station's " +
          "previous reading, less the share where it fell"
    }</span>
    ${missing}
  </div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// One line a chain: how its readings split between a fall, a rise and no move.
changesSummary = {
  const rows = changesPlace === "All US states" ? changesByState : changesByStation;
  const totals = new Map();
  for (const row of rows) {
    const t = totals.get(row.brand) || {obs: 0, changed: 0, up: 0, down: 0};
    t.obs += Number(row.n_obs) || 0;
    t.changed += Number(row.n_changed) || 0;
    t.up += Number(row.n_up) || 0;
    t.down += Number(row.n_down) || 0;
    totals.set(row.brand, t);
  }
  const share = (n, t) => fmtShare((n / t.obs) * 100);
  const lines = [...totals.entries()]
    .sort()
    .filter(([, t]) => t.obs > 0)
    .map(
      ([brand, t]) =>
        html`<div>${BRAND_NAMES[brand] || brand}: ${share(t.down, t)} fell · ${share(
          t.up,
          t
        )} rose · ${share(t.obs - t.changed, t)} unchanged, of ${changesCount(
          t.obs,
          "reading"
        )}</div>`
    );
  return lines.length ? html`<div class="cgp-notice cgp-changes-summary">${lines}</div>` : "";
}
```
